clue.text: Pop suffering? Yes (in genitals)

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the words that follow are knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the brackets only disguise these as an aside

explanation.surface: A cheeky medical complaint: pop music that hurts, with a 'yes' tucked into the groin.
explanation.walkthrough: All thirteen letters of 'Yes in genitals' are the fodder; the brackets just make the surface read as a rude aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy listening is a genre of undemanding popular music, so it is a kind of pop.

clue.text: Speak suddenly of alimony?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cry out abruptly
second, punning meaning: alimony is a claim made by a former spouse

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as EX CLAIM: alimony is what an ex claims. The question mark flags this whimsical second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to call out suddenly, as in surprise or strong feeling.

clue.text: Got ready to fight boringly orthodox political party

parts.note: a square is a conventional, unfashionable person
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A conventional, dull party bracing itself for a political scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party, a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to adopt a fighting stance and face an opponent, so the past tense means prepared for a fight.

clue.text: Language school at Innsbruck folds

indicators.note: to fold is to enclose, so the phrase before it wraps the answer inside itself

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of school, all of at and the start of Innsbruck

explanation.surface: A language school in the Austrian city of Innsbruck goes out of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome, still studied at school.

clue.text: Military chaplain knowingly discharged loaded pistol outside

indicators.note: the reshuffled weapon sits on the outside, wrapped around the emptied word
loaded in the sense of drunk, so the next word staggers into a new order
discharged means emptied, so the inside of the word goes and only its two ends stay

parts.note: first and last letters once the middle is emptied out
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An army padre deliberately fires a loaded gun out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged pistol is split after its first letter to take in the emptied word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is old slang for a clergyman, especially a forces chaplain, as one who steers souls heavenward.

clue.text: MENSA could be made completely free to enrich the inner spirit

indicators.note: freed completely means set loose at both ends, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the society name with its outer letters dropped
the word with its outer letters dropped

explanation.surface: The high-IQ society might be opened to all, nourishing everyone's inner life.
explanation.walkthrough: Mensa is the society for people with high IQs. Even the blogger found this one forced: 'could be' must be read as the word could, to be stripped.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensoul is to give something a soul, that is, to fill it with spiritual life.

clue.text: Bury row going on between finance houses

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
a bank is a row, as of switches, oars or keys

explanation.surface: Bury, the Lancashire town, has a quarrel running between its financial institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Bury suggests the English town; it is the verb. 'Row' wants to be a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Interbank describes dealings such as loans made directly between banks, which are finance houses.

clue.text: Golf clubs left incomplete sign directing players

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is short of its final letter

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A golfer's clubs left lying around, and a sign telling players where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf clubs' reads as a set of sticks, but each word gives its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A G clef is the treble clef, a musical symbol telling performers which pitch each stave line stands for.

clue.text: Good part of ladder standing on earth/dirt

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a rung is one step of a ladder
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A good ladder rung planted in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'standing on' puts the earlier pieces above the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunge is dirt or grime, chiefly in American use, before it named the music style.

clue.text: Nobleman clearing rocky land

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

indicators.note: clearing a word empties out its middle, so only its first and last letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters once the inside is cleared

explanation.surface: An aristocrat clears stones from his rough, rocky estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a nation's land, its territory, as in 'a hilly country'.

clue.text: Line penned by Julius that decides the argument

indicators.note: something penned is shut in a pen, so the letter sits inside the word that follows

parts.note: Julius is this puzzle's setter, naming himself
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A clinching line written by the setter Julius settles a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often refer to themselves; here Julius, the pseudonym of this crossword's compiler, stands for the word for his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a remark or blow that settles a matter conclusively, a clincher.

clue.text: Protective clothing article worn by professional

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone goes around them, so the article wraps the next word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A garment or protective item put on by a skilled worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an item of clothing, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment tied over the front to keep clothes clean, so it is protective wear.

clue.text: Decline for pub industry, about to take medicine?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the concealed letters are read from right to left
to take in is to hold, so the letters sit inside the phrase before

parts.note: the end of Decline, then for and pub whole, then the first letter of industry

explanation.surface: A slump in the pub trade, enough to give anyone a headache that needs a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the answer is one particular medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling drug, an example of a medicine.

clue.text: Mediocre puzzle to do with fashion from Spooner?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two key words change places

parts.note: a puzzle is a riddle and a fashion is a mode; swapping the opening sounds gives the phrase

explanation.surface: A dull crossword about the fashion world, as Reverend Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: After the swap, the second word sounds like rode, spelt as the word for a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road means moderate and unadventurous, hence ordinary or mediocre.

clue.text: Reform leaflet featuring nothing new ignored

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A political leaflet about reform with nothing fresh in it gets ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' suggests a political campaign, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left alone is not touched or bothered, so it has been ignored.

clue.text: Motor home?

parts.note: surface reading: a camper van or mobile home
setter's reading: the home where a motor car lives

explanation.walkthrough: Solvers expect a vehicle you live in, or a double definition; it is the building where a car is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is the building where a car is housed, so it is literally a car's home.

clue.text: Accommodation suitable for housing painting chaps?

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so the word wraps the pieces that follow

parts.note: apt means fitting or suitable
painting is a form of art
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Lodgings ideal for putting up a group of painter-decorators.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms to live in, so it is a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Where jarheads learn combat op manoeuvres?

indicators.note: manoeuvres are moves, so the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Where US Marines are taught fighting operations and military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarhead is American slang for a US Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot camp is the training camp where new military recruits, such as marines, learn the basics.

clue.text: Rent high, which is a swindle

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
meat that is high has gone off

explanation.surface: Steep rents complained of as daylight robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as money paid to a landlord; it is the noun for a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-off is a fraud or an exorbitant charge, so it is a swindle.

clue.text: Keen to go north to sample Glasgow's premier music genre

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word is turned around
to sample is to take some in, so the turned word takes the letter inside

parts.note: eager means keen

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of the city is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the city

explanation.surface: Someone eager to travel north and try Glasgow's top music style.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae is the Jamaican popular music style, a genre of music.

clue.text: How to make last halite?

indicators.note: the clue asks for an instruction that would produce the given word, so the answer itself contains the shuffling command

parts.note: to rock is to shake about, the instruction the answer gives
these four letters, which the instruction would shake into the clue's word

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about how to make a mineral endure.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read the answer as an instruction, rock (shake) the second word, and the result is the clue's 'last'.
explanation.definitionFit: Halite is the mineral name for natural sodium chloride, mined as common salt in crystal form.

clue.text: See 13
Work to support trendy husband in cultural movement

parts.note: hip means fashionable
H is the abbreviation for husband
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A man takes a job to support his fashionable husband within an arts scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that supports the others sits beneath them, so the work comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop is a youth culture of rap, DJing, breakdancing and graffiti, a cultural movement.

clue.text: I start running after you punched Joe Strummer

indicators.note: something punched has a hole made in it, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: GI Joe is a US soldier, so GI is a Joe
U sounds like you, as in text speak

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move and out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Joe Strummer of The Clash wakes with a jolt after being hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joe Strummer' reads as the punk musician of The Clash, but Joe is the soldier and only 'Strummer' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A strummer is someone who sweeps a hand across the strings, which is what a guitar player does.

clue.text: Dignitary regularly falls over opening bars

indicators.note: letters falling away at regular intervals means every other one drops out

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An important official keeps tripping over at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, and O is its scorebook abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the introductory passage of a song, its opening bars.

clue.text: Joint e-mail Tories periodically despatched

indicators.note: letters sent away at regular periods leaves every other one behind

parts.note: the even-placed letters, ignoring the hyphen and space

explanation.surface: An email to Conservative MPs sent out at intervals, with a hint of a shared venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a woodworking joint where two pieces meet at an angle, as at a picture frame corner.

clue.text: Such as iron supplement finally put in breakfast?

indicators.note: something put in another thing goes inside it

parts.note: breakfast is a meal

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: An iron supplement taken with the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: iron is one such thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a chemical element of the metal class, so it is an example of a metal.

clue.text: Ancient city against introduction of Ottoman church

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An old city resists the arrival of an Ottoman church.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was an ancient city founded by the Seleucids, near modern Antakya in Turkey.

clue.text: Unwrapped box containing diamonds, Eastern Cape style

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the trimmed word goes around what follows
something unwrapped has its outer covering removed, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a carton is a box
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
EC is the abbreviation for Eastern Cape, a South African province

explanation.surface: Opening a box of diamonds from South Africa's Eastern Cape, a stylish gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eastern Cape is a province of South Africa, abbreviated EC.

clue.text: "Very crowded, poor" — Upper Volta in dictionary

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumble goes within the dictionary's letters
poor in the sense of in bad shape, so the letters of the former country's name are jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters rearranged
the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A quoted dictionary description of Upper Volta as crowded and poor.
explanation.walkthrough: Upper Volta is the former name of Burkina Faso in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Overpopulated means having too many inhabitants for the area, so very crowded.
